hints: The probability of having a birthday on Saturday is p = 1/7, and not on Saturday is q = 6/7.
For 10 people, let X ~ B(10, 1/7). None having a birthday on Saturday means X = 0.
walkthrough:
Model the number of Saturday birthdays among 10 people as $X \sim B\left(10, \frac{1}{7}\right)$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 0) = \left(\frac{6}{7}\right)^{10} = \frac{60466176}{282475249} \approx 0.214\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Model definition:
Each day of the week is equally likely, so for any individual, the probability of a birthday on Saturday is $p = \frac{1}{7}$, and the probability of not on Saturday is $q = \frac{6}{7}$.
For $n = 10$ independent people, let $X$ be the number having a Saturday birthday:
$$X \sim B\left(10, \frac{1}{7}\right)$$

hints: Fewer than 3 people means X = 0, 1, or 2.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the event:
With $X \sim B\left(10, \frac{1}{7}\right)$, fewer than 3 people means:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 3) = \mathrm{P}(X = 0) + \mathrm{P}(X = 1) + \mathrm{P}(X = 2)$$

Step 3: Sum the terms:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 3) = 0.214058 + 0.356764 + 0.267573 = 0.838395\dots$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.838$.

ai_rubric.Calculating Binomial Tail Probabilities: Sums binomial terms for X = 0, 1, 2 to obtain 0.838.

hints: Model: X ~ B(392, 1/7). Check conditions: np = 392/7 = 56 > 5 and nq = 392 * (6/7) = 336 > 5.
Approximating normal parameters: mu = 56, variance sigma^2 = 56 * (6/7) = 48, so sigma = sqrt(48) = 6.928.
Apply continuity correction to more than 60 people (X >= 61): P(X > 60) corresponds to Y > 60.5.
walkthrough:
Verify normal approximation conditions for $X \sim B\left(392, \frac{1}{7}\right)$:
$$np = 392 \times \frac{1}{7} = 56 > 5, \quad nq = 392 \times \frac{6}{7} = 336 > 5$$

Calculate parameters for the approximating normal distribution $Y$:
$$\mu = 56, \quad \sigma = \sqrt{npq} = \sqrt{392 \times \frac{1}{7} \times \frac{6}{7}} = \sqrt{48} \approx 6.9282$$

Apply the continuity correction for more than 60 people ($X \ge 61$):
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 60) = \mathrm{P}(X \ge 61) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y > 60.5)$$

Standardise and evaluate the upper-tail probability:
$$Z = \frac{60.5 - 56}{\sqrt{48}} = \frac{4.5}{6.9282} \approx 0.650$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.650) = 1 - \Phi(0.650) = 1 - 0.7422 = 0.2578 \approx 0.258\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Check conditions for a normal approximation:
$$X \sim B\left(392, \frac{1}{7}\right)$$
$$np = 392 \times \frac{1}{7} = 56 > 5$$
$$nq = 392 \times \frac{6}{7} = 336 > 5$$
Both conditions are satisfied, justifying a normal approximation $Y \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$.

Step 2: Calculate mean and standard deviation:
$$\mu = np = 56$$
$$\sigma^2 = npq = 56 \times \frac{6}{7} = 48$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{48} \approx 6.92820$$

Step 3: Continuity correction:
We require $\mathrm{P}(X > 60)$. In integers, $X > 60$ is $X \ge 61$.
The discrete value $61$ corresponds to the continuous interval $[60.5, 61.5]$.
Thus $X \ge 61$ becomes:
$$Y > 60.5$$

Step 5: Compute the upper-tail probability:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.650) = 1 - \Phi(0.650) = 1 - 0.7422 = 0.2578$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.258$.

ai_rubric.Applying a Normal Approximation: Computes mu = 56, sigma = sqrt(48), uses continuity correction 60.5, standardises to 0.650, and finds 0.258.
